model_output.verdict: Google and Dell Technologies catch my eye, and the program results under both back up the names. I’d hesitate over the current Operations Manager role because I can’t tell how big the terminal operation or your team is.
write_up: You’ve moved from supply chain programs at Dell Technologies to data center capacity planning at Google and now terminal operations at Brightline Freight Partners. It’s common for a current role to be described in broad duties, but these lines won’t stand out in a pile for operations jobs. A recruiter can see what you managed before, not yet what you manage at Brightline.

The Google line about cutting the forecast-to-delivery cycle is your best model: it names the change, the before and after, and the decision that made it possible. Your earlier roles also show budgets, suppliers and team leadership. The Brightline role needs comparable detail to show what you do now.

Let’s start with the Austin terminal line, then add the team count and the work your coordinators and dispatchers handle. Name the carrier issues and weekly measures too. Those details can bring your current role up to the standard set by the earlier ones.

cards.line: - Responsible for daily operations of the Austin terminal
cards.cannot_tell: A recruiter can’t tell what the terminal handles or how much activity you’re responsible for. That makes the current operation difficult to compare with your earlier programs.
cards.example: Responsible for daily operations of the Austin terminal, including [work] for [volume of activity]
cards.question: What daily operations are yours, and how much activity does the terminal handle?

cards.line: - Manage a team of coordinators and dispatchers
cards.cannot_tell: You name the team, but not how many people are on it or what they handle. Both matter when a recruiter is considering you for another management role.
cards.example: Manage a team of [number] coordinators and dispatchers who [team responsibilities]
cards.question: How many coordinators and dispatchers do you manage, and what does the team handle?

cards.line: - Work with carriers and customers to resolve issues
cards.cannot_tell: The carrier and customer work is relevant, but the issues and your part in resolving them are still a blank.
cards.example: Work with carriers and customers to resolve [types of issues] by [your actions]
cards.question: What issues do you resolve with carriers and customers, and what do you do to resolve them?

cards.line: - Report weekly metrics to the regional director
cards.cannot_tell: The reporting cadence and audience are clear. The measures and the decisions they inform aren’t named.
cards.example: Report weekly metrics on [measures] to the regional director for [decisions]
cards.question: Which measures do you report, and what decisions do they inform?

cards.line: - Cut the forecast-to-delivery cycle for new capacity from 14 months to 9 by consolidating three approval tracks into one
cards.cannot_tell: Keep this as a model. It connects your own action to a concrete change without making the reader guess how the work got done.

fit.why: Your current title and work managing the Austin terminal point most directly to another Operations Manager role.
fit.note: Your earlier program work gives you a useful background in supply chain and capacity planning. Put the same detail around the terminal operation to show how that experience carries into your current work.
